items.title: Panama Francis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995
items.q: here comes Cannonball and George Kelly and all the rest of them, then everybody followed me up there.

ctx.x: Tell us some of the big bands that you played with. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -5-

Well I started out with a band in Miami when I was fourteen years old, called George Kelly and the Cavaliers. And I was with them until I was eighteen, and I went to Tampa to join a band that was fronted by a guy named Charlie Brantley. And then I left and went to New York. And I did something in New York that very few musicians or very few people in show business have done. I got to New York on a Tuesday and went to work Sunday and I never looked back. I was like one of the first ones of my peers to leave home.…
Tell us about how it was like, the travel, the pay, the lifestyle of working with the traveling band.

items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: Mr. Leander Kirksey, Kurtzin who was responsible for Nat Adderley and Cannonball Adderley

ctx.x: And my mother used to take me there

and wait for me until the end of the night and bring me home.

And I'll never forget the first song I ever played -- it was "Blue Prelude"; we played that, and we used to play "Dinah" and "Sweet Sue" and "One Sweet Letter from You" and all those types of tunes then.

So I stayed there, and there was a band -- I was still in school at the time, and there was a band with a bunch of school kids that was under the direction of Mr. Leander Kirksey, Kurtzin who was responsible for Nat Adderley and Cannonball Adderley,…
hear from now -- he's a minister, a big minister in Alabama, Arthur Duncan was one of the trumpet players. And there was Morris Meadows ...
